claims.claim: Under the same fed-state condition, ziprasidone reached approximately 59-60% absolute oral bioavailability when dosed after a high-fat meal, demonstrating that a lipophilic, poorly water-soluble drug can meet the F>=20% threshold in the fed state.

Sertindole, another lipophilic piperazine antipsychotic, has an oral bioavailability of about 74-75% and its absorption is not significantly affected by food, indicating that high lipophilicity and neutral character do not preclude F>=20%.

Other L1 records with moderate or first-pass-limited bioavailability (apixaban 49%, diltiazem 38%, aPPD 37%, and an allometric prediction of 23%) all remain at or above the 20% threshold, so no transferable record supports F<20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral-bioavailability record for the query structure (itraconazole-type azole) is present in the supplied cards.
No measured solubility, permeability, or first-pass data for the query are supplied; the low prior is physicochemical only.
The fed-state effect for the query is inferred from ziprasidone high-fat-meal and sertindole food-effect records rather than measured in the query.
content.decision_summary: Although the physicochemical prior is unfavorable, all transferable L1 records report F>=20%, and the fed-state ziprasidone records (~59-60% absolute F after a high-fat meal) plus sertindole records (~74-75%, food-insensitive) support that this lipophilic azole can meet the F>=20% threshold; predict high with moderate confidence.
